content:
Let \(x\) be the number of triangular faces and \(y\) the number of pentagonal faces, so
\[
x+y=32.
\]
Separate vertex-face incidences:
\[
3x=VT,\qquad 5y=VP.
\]
Thus
\[
\frac{VT}{3}+\frac{VP}{5}=32
\]
so
\[
V(5T+3P)=480.
\]
From Euler and edge-counting,
\[
V=\frac{3x+5y}{2}-30=\frac{V(T+P)}{2}-30,
\]
so
\[
V(T+P-2)=60.
\]
Dividing the two equations gives
\[
\frac{5T+3P}{T+P-2}=8.
\]
Hence
\[
5T+3P=8T+8P-16
\]
so
\[
3T+5P=16.
\]
The nonnegative integer solution is \(T=2,\ P=2\). Then
\[
V(4-2)=60 \implies V=30.
\]
Therefore,
\[
100P+10T+V=100(2)+10(2)+30=250.
\]
\[
\boxed{250}
\]
